'''''Beschorneria yuccoides''''' is a [[species]] of [[succulent plant]] belonging to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]], subfamily [[Agavoideae]].

==Etymology==
The [[epithet]] ''yuccoides'' is a compound of the botanical name of the genus ''[[Yucca]]'' and the [[Greek language|Greek]] suffix -ό-εἶδος (''o-eidos'')  ''oides'' meaning "likeness".<ref>Urs Eggli, Leonard E. Newton: ''Etymological Dictionary of Succulent Plant Names''. Springer, Berlin/Heidelberg 2010, {{ISBN|978-3-642-05597-3}}, S. 263.</ref>

==Subspecies==
* ''Beschorneria yuccoides subsp. yuccoides''
* ''Beschorneria yuccoides subsp. dekosteriana'' (K.Koch) Govaerts

==Description==
[[File:Asparagaceae - Beschorneria yuccoides.JPG|thumb|right|Blooms of ''Beschorneria yuccoides'']]
''Beschorneria yuccoides'' is a stemless plant with 20 to 35 linear, lanceolate, leathery leaves that are widened at their base. They are gray-green to green, about {{convert|40|-|60|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3.3|-|3.5|cm|abbr=on}} wide. The leaf margins are finely denticulate. The [[inflorescence]] reaches a height of {{convert|100|-|180|cm|abbr=on}}, with a maximum of {{convert|320 |cm|in|abbr=on}}. The stem and the bract are red. The [[flower]]s are 40 to 50 mm long. The fruits are elongated to almost spherical, {{convert|30|-|40|mm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|15|-|25|mm|abbr=on}} wide.<ref>RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants. United Kingdom: Dorling Kindersley. 2008. p. 1136. {{ISBN|1405332964}}</ref><ref name=germ>{{GRIN | accessdate = 23 January 2018}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''Beschorneria yuccoides'' is present in [[Mexico]],<ref name=eol>[http://eol.org/pages/1086235/overview Encyclopedia of Life]</ref> in the states of [[Hidalgo (state)|Hidalgo]], [[Puebla]] and [[Veracruz]], at an elevation of {{convert|2700|-|3000|m|abbr=on}} above sea level.<ref name=eggli>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1bjwYOO_Zt0C&dq=Beschorneria+yuccoides+hidalgo+puebla+veracruz&pg=PA77|title=Illustrated Handbook of Succulent Plants: Monocotyledons|date=17 July 2001|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|last=Eggli|first=Urs|isbn=9783540416920 }}</ref>

==Cultivation==
This plant is not tolerant of severe freezes, and is best suited to warm, sheltered south- or west-facing places in full sun, where temperatures do not fall below {{convert|-5|C|F}}. Alternatively, it can be grown under glass.

It grows outdoors at Earlscliffe, [[Howth]], [[County Dublin]], Ireland, at a latitude of 53.3º N, where it benefits from the unusually favourable microclimate.<ref>{{cite web
| url= http://www.earlscliffe.com/plants_that_grow_well.htm
| title= Plants that thrive at Earlscliffe'
| publisher= Earlscliffe
| accessdate= 15 May 2018
| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180516103026/http://www.earlscliffe.com/plants_that_grow_well.htm
| archive-date= 16 May 2018
| url-status= dead
}}</ref>

In cultivation in the [[United Kingdom|UK]] it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/27870/i-Beschorneria-yuccoides-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Beschorneria yuccoides''
| publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate=12 January 2018}}</ref>
